# AD Photography

> Solo Toronto wedding photographer for intimate ceremonies. Candid, cinematic wedding and pre-wedding photography across the GTA; films offered for pre-wedding sessions.

AD Photography is a solo Toronto-based wedding and pre-wedding photography practice serving the Greater Toronto Area and all of Canada. It specializes in candid, cinematic, editorial-style wedding photography (photo-only on wedding days), pre-wedding photo and film sessions, civil ceremonies, and celebrations.

## Positioning

Solo photographer operation, not a large studio. Intentionally focused on intimate, unhurried weddings, church weddings, civil ceremonies, small receptions, pre-wedding stories. Not a multi-shooter Indian/South Asian wedding specialist. Style is candid and cinematic with light prompting rather than posed set-ups.

## Packages

### Pre-Wedding
- Love Story Mini: $351.25 (up to 2 hours, 1 location, 50+ edited photos)
- Love Story + Film: $551.25 (3-4 hours, 1 location, 40 edited photos, 2-3 minute 4K film)
- Love Story Duo: $551.25 (up to 3 hours, 2 locations, 2 outfit changes, 80+ edited photos)
- The Signature Session: $751.25 (on sale, regularly $851.25, up to 5 hours, 2 locations, 2 outfit changes, 70+ edited photos, 3-4 minute 4K film)
- The Pre Wedding: $1,251.25 (on sale, regularly $1,451.25, up to 10 hours, 3 locations, 3 outfit changes, 150+ edited photos, 5-7 minute custom 4K film + 30-40 second trailer/save-the-date)
- The Weekend Away: $1,501.25 (a full weekend, 150+ edited photos, 5 to 7 minute custom 4K film plus a 30 to 40 second trailer)

### Wedding
- The Essentials: $1,401.25 (up to 6 hours, 200+ edited photos, engagement session included)
- The Full Day: $2,301.25 (on sale, regularly $2,501.25, up to 10 hours, 400+ edited photos, engagement session included, second photographer included)
- The Complete Story: $3,801.25 (up to 14 hours, 600+ edited photos, engagement session included, second photographer included)

### Civil Ceremony & Elopements
- The Civil Ceremony: $501.25 (up to 2 hours, 150+ edited photos)
- The Elopement: $901.25 (up to 4 hours, 250+ edited photos)

### Celebrations
- The Hourly: $100 (book by the hour, 40 edited per hour photos)
- Celebrations: $551.25 (minimum 2 hours, Unlimited edited photos)

### Custom
- Make It Yours: Custom pricing. Start from any package above and customize locations, hours, and coverage.

## Location Guides

- [Allan Gardens Conservatory](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/allan-gardens/): Tropical palms under Victorian glass, warm and quiet no matter what Toronto's weather is doing outside.
- [Art Gallery of Hamilton](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/art-gallery-hamilton/): A modern gallery in Hamilton's downtown core where bold lines and plaza light do the editorial work.
- [Bayfront Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/bayfront-park/): An open stretch of Hamilton waterfront where soft lake light meets greenery right at the city's edge.
- [Casa Loma](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/casa-loma/): A stone castle above midtown Toronto, manicured gardens at its feet and the skyline beyond.
- [Cherry Beach](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/cherry-beach/): A rough stretch of city beach in the Port Lands with the whole Toronto skyline sitting across open water.
- [Distillery District](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/distillery-district/): Car-free cobblestone lanes and brick warehouses that feel like old Europe, right in downtown Toronto.
- [Dundas Peak](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/dundas-peak/): Tree-tunnel light on the hike in, then a cliff edge over a valley that goes full orange in the fall.
- [Evergreen Brick Works](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/evergreen-brick-works/): An old brickworks in the Don Valley where reclaimed industrial brick and green quarry trails share one frame.
- [Graffiti Alley](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/graffiti-alley/): A narrow Queen West laneway painted end to end, loud colour on every wall that cuts hard against clean styling.
- [Guild Park & Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/guild-park/): Stone columns rescued from demolished Toronto buildings, standing in a garden that feels like old Europe.
- [High Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/high-park/): A sprawling park that turns pink with cherry blossoms each spring and burns red along the lake every fall.
- [Humber Arboretum](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/humber-arboretum/): Winding forest trails that open onto the Humber, green and quiet enough to forget you're still in Toronto.
- [Humber Bay Arch Bridge](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/humber-bay-arch-bridge/): A sculptural arch over the lake that frames couples against the skyline as the sun goes down.
- [Kortright Centre for Conservation](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/kortright-centre/): Forest trails and pond boardwalks in Vaughan, quiet enough that strangers rarely wander into the frame.
- [Toronto Music Garden](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/music-garden/): Winding garden paths and ornamental grasses at the water's edge, with the downtown towers rising right behind.
- [Niagara Parks Botanical Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/niagara-botanical-gardens/): Forty hectares of sculpted gardens that feel more like Europe than Niagara, especially on a quiet weekday.
- [Niagara-on-the-Lake](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/niagara-on-the-lake/): Flower boxes and colonial storefronts down to the lake, the closest Ontario gets to a storybook village.
- [Osgoode Hall](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/osgoode-hall/): Neoclassical columns and manicured lawns behind iron gates that were built to keep cattle out.
- [Polson Pier](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/polson-pier/): A flat paved pier across the inner harbour where the whole Toronto skyline lines up in one frame.
- [Queen Victoria Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/queen-victoria-park/): Green parkland facing Horseshoe Falls, with mist hanging in the air and rainbows on sunny days.
- [RC Harris Water Treatment Center](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rc-harris/): A 1930s Art Deco waterworks above the lake that makes two people look like a film still without trying.
- [Royal Botanical Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/royal-botanical-gardens/): A quiet sprawl of gardens and woodland trails where the blooms are never the same two visits in a row.
- [Scarborough Bluffs](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/scarborough-bluffs/): White clay cliffs over a sandy beach, the closest thing Toronto has to a destination coastline.
- [TD Dominion Centre / King St](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/td-centre/): Mies van der Rohe's towers and a King Street streetcar rolling past, the city at its most cinematic.
- [Toronto Islands](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/toronto-islands/): A short ferry ride to quiet beaches and cottage lanes, with the full Toronto skyline across the water.
- [University of Toronto](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/uoft/): Gothic cloisters and century-old stone that feel like Oxford dropped into downtown Toronto.
- [Webster's Falls](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/websters-falls/): A waterfall in the Dundas forest that you hear before you see, with mist drifting all the way up the trail.
- [Dundurn Castle](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/dundurn-castle/): An 1830s Italianate villa above Hamilton Harbour that reads like a European estate, an hour from Toronto.
- [Spencer Smith Park and Burlington Village](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/burlington-village/): The curve of Brant Street Pier over open water, and cobblestone village streets a five-minute stroll away.
- [Adamson Estate](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/adamson-estate/): A 1919 stone manor where the late light comes off Lake Ontario and warms the ivy and the lawn.
- [Aera Toronto](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/aera-toronto/): A modern Italian dining room 38 floors over downtown that turns candle-warm just as the skyline lights up.
- [St. Patrick's Catholic Parish](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/st-patricks-parish-hamilton/): An 1877 stone Gothic Revival church with a painted starry-blue vault and a rose window that lights the centre aisle.
- [Union Station Great Hall](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/union-station/): Warm Missouri stone, windows four storeys tall, and a herringbone marble floor the whole city walks across.
- [Kariya Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/kariya-park/): A pocket of Japan behind the Mississauga towers, nearly eighty cherry trees and a still pond that goes quiet the moment you step through the gate.
- [Cheltenham Badlands](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/cheltenham-badlands/): Rust red shale hills rolling away from a boardwalk in Caledon, a landscape that looks like it wandered in from another province.
- [Nathan Phillips Square](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/nathan-phillips-square/): Curved white towers, three concrete arches over the pool, and a sign that lights up after dark. Downtown Toronto at its most graphic.
- [Trinity Bellwoods Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/trinity-bellwoods/): Stone college gates on Queen West, then big open lawns, old shade trees, and the white squirrels this neighbourhood is quietly famous for.
- [Sugar Beach](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/sugar-beach/): Candy pink umbrellas over white sand on a former parking lot, with the working Redpath sugar refinery right across the slip.
- [Canoe Landing Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/canoe-landing/): I still climb the berm for this one. The red canoe that crowned it burned in 2025, but the view it framed is intact, Gardiner below, CityPlace glass behind.
- [Riverdale Park East](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/riverdale-park-east/): A wide grass hill above the Don Valley, with the downtown towers stacked across the ravine and catching the last low light of the day.
- [Trillium Park at Ontario Place](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/trillium-park/): A stone ravine stamped with moccasin prints opens straight onto Lake Ontario, and the skyline sits at the end of the trail.
- [Fort York National Historic Site](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/fort-york/): A War of 1812 garrison of earth ramparts, stone magazines and timber blockhouses, with the Gardiner overhead and glass towers right behind.
- [Royal Ontario Museum](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rom/): Libeskind's aluminum and glass shards cut over Bloor Street, and right behind them the original museum keeps its quiet stone galleries.
- [Art Gallery of Ontario](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/ago/): A spiral staircase in Douglas fir winding up through a glass ceiling, and a blue titanium wing looking out over Grange Park.
- [Ripley's Aquarium of Canada](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/ripleys-aquarium/): I love what the tunnel does to faces here, deep blue light washing over both of you while sharks and turtles drift past overhead.
- [Fairmont Royal York](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/fairmont-royal-york/): A 1929 railway hotel facing Union Station, carved wood ceilings and crystal chandeliers in the lobby, and a Ballroom restored to its 1929 decor.
- [One King West Hotel](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/one-king-west/): A 1914 Dominion Bank vault under the Financial District, forty tonnes of steel door standing open at the foot of a marble staircase.
- [Pantages Hotel](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/pantages-hotel/): A third floor event space that overlooks Massey Hall and fills with natural light, so winter portraits stay warm without ever stepping outside.
- [Sunnyside Pavilion](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/sunnyside-pavilion/): A 1922 Beaux Arts bathing pavilion where columns and a wide archway open straight onto the boardwalk, Lake Ontario filling the whole background.
- [Spadina Museum](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/spadina-museum/): A 5.7 acre estate garden in Casa Loma's shadow, grounds restored to their early 1900s look, apple orchard and grape arbour behind the house.
- [Todmorden Mills Heritage Site](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/todmorden-mills/): An 1820s mill village hidden under the Don Valley walls, warm brick and a lone smokestack, with the city nowhere in the frame.
- [Taylor Creek Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/taylor-creek/): A long green ravine under East York, where a paved trail crosses the creek on wooden and steel bridges while the city goes quiet above you.
- [Serena Gundy Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/serena-gundy/): A West Don ravine where the canopy closes over the trail and every clearing catches a different angle of afternoon light.
- [Sunnybrook Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/sunnybrook/): Horses in the paddocks, wide meadows on the Don flats, and old trees along the river, with almost no city in view.
- [Edwards Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/edwards-gardens/): Terraced flower beds stepping down into the Wilket Creek ravine, with a footbridge over the creek at the bottom.
- [Aga Khan Museum](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/aga-khan-museum/): Brazilian granite and still reflecting pools set out in perfect geometry. I shoot the reflections first, then work the formal garden as the light drops.
- [Alexander Muir Memorial Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/alexander-muir-gardens/): Rose beds stepping down a hillside in stone terraces, a maple leaf gate on Yonge, and a ravine waiting at the bottom of the stairs.
- [Earl Bales Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/earl-bales/): An open amphitheatre on the plateau, and a few steps behind it the ground drops away into the wooded slopes of the West Don ravine.
- [G. Ross Lord Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/g-ross-lord/): Wide meadow grass that goes gold by late summer, a reservoir holding the last of the light, and enough open sky to forget the city is right there.
- [Glendon Campus, York University](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/glendon-campus/): A 1920s Italian style villa on the brow of the Don ravine, with a rose garden and century old trees spread across the lawns.
- [York University, Keele Campus](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/york-university/): A 1992 orange brick rotunda, a reflecting pool, and a colonnaded promenade that holds soft even light the whole way down the Common.
- [Black Creek Pioneer Village](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/black-creek-village/): Forty heritage buildings on a gravel main street, an 1860s Ontario town rebuilt whole, with very little modern creeping into the back of the frame.
- [Bluffer's Park and Beach](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/bluffers-park/): Masts in the marina basin, open sand past it, and the clay cliffs of the Bluffs standing over the whole park.
- [Rosetta McClain Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rosetta-mcclain/): A formal garden on the edge of the Scarborough Bluffs. Raised beds, roses, a vine covered trellis, and Lake Ontario filling the horizon.
- [Colonel Danforth Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/colonel-danforth/): Highland Creek cuts a wooded ravine through Scarborough, and I can walk a couple onto a forest path here with nothing else in the frame.
- [Miller Lash House](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/miller-lash-house/): A 1913 fieldstone summer estate on a knoll above Highland Creek, with wooded valley on three sides and the UTSC campus up the hill.
- [University of Toronto Scarborough](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/utsc/): I love the contrast here. Poured concrete stepping along the ravine edge, then a forested creek valley a short walk below it.
- [Rouge National Urban Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rouge-park/): Among the largest urban parks in North America, a forested river valley with a two level lookout, the one place near Toronto I can frame as nothing but wild.
- [Port Credit Memorial Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/port-credit/): The Credit River bending down toward the harbour, boats moving out past the marina, and the white lighthouse a short walk over the bridge.
- [Rattray Marsh Conservation Area](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rattray-marsh/): Boardwalk winding through open marsh, then a shingle beach where Lake Ontario opens up. The most untouched shoreline I shoot in the GTA.
- [The Riverwood Conservancy](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/riverwood/): A 1919 house with Arts and Crafts gardens set around a lily pond, and a walk downhill behind it where the Credit River woods close in.
- [Brueckner Rhododendron Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/brueckner-rhododendron/): Eighteen acres of rhododendrons under tall white pines, sloping down to a quiet stretch of Lake Ontario shoreline at the foot of the garden.
- [Lakefront Promenade Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/lakefront-promenade/): I shoot this one facing the water. Sailboat masts on one side, the small red and white beacon out on the breakwater, open lake behind you.
- [Chinguacousy Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/chinguacousy-park/): A hundred acres in Bramalea where formal flower beds meet a pond bridge, and a glass tropical house stays green through February.
- [Gage Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/gage-park-brampton/): Brampton's oldest park, opened in 1903, with a bandstand near its centre and mature trees breaking the late light across the flower beds.
- [Heart Lake Conservation Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/heart-lake/): A kettle lake the glaciers left behind, ringed by forest and planted pine rows, still enough most mornings to hold your reflection off the shore.
- [Peel Art Gallery Museum and Archives (PAMA)](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/pama/): An 1867 county courthouse and jail in downtown Brampton, where the old courtroom and the heavy stone exterior sit a few steps apart.
- [Belfountain Conservation Area](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/belfountain/): The bridge sways a little when you cross it, the falls run right underneath, and the old stone fountain waits on the far bank.
- [Forks of the Credit Provincial Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/forks-of-the-credit/): Rolling escarpment hills and a kettle lake minutes from the trailhead. The waterfall sits deeper in the gorge, and I think it's worth the walk.
- [Alton Mill Arts Centre](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/alton-mill/): An 1881 stone knitting mill on Shaw's Creek, artist studios still working inside and the old mill pond lying quiet behind the walls.
- [Terra Cotta Conservation Area](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/terra-cotta/): Wolf Lake and the sugar bush on one easy loop, a boardwalk over restored wetland, and the main Bruce Trail route climbing the escarpment behind it.
- [Boyd Conservation Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/boyd-conservation/): Old hemlocks, a steep valley, the East Humber running through it. I like that you park close and still shoot like you drove two hours north.
- [Kleinburg Village Main Street](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/kleinburg-main-street/): Old village houses turned into shops line the east side of Islington Avenue, set close enough that one slow walk gives you several backdrops.
- [McMichael Canadian Art Collection](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/mcmichael/): One hundred acres of Group of Seven woodland around a hewn log gallery, bronze sculptures hiding along the paths, and a ridgetop over the Humber.
- [Eagles Nest Golf Club](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/eagles-nest/): A links style course of rolling fairways and fescue north of the city, with a lower patio built for outdoor ceremonies and sunset views.
- [Copper Creek Golf Club](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/copper-creek/): A copper roofed clubhouse above the Humber River Valley, with a stone gazebo and a terrace where the last hour of light runs long and gold.
- [The Doctor's House](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/doctors-house/): A wooden pew chapel with cathedral windows and its own bell, set in the gardens of a 19th century Kleinburg house that backs onto the Humber.
- [Main Street Unionville](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/unionville-main-street/): Painted 1800s shopfronts, a bandstand on the corner, Toogood Pond just north. I walk this whole street slowly and it never runs out of frames.
- [Toogood Pond Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/toogood-pond/): Willows along the shoreline, a boardwalk through the cattails, and Unionville's heritage Main Street a short walk from the north entrance.
- [Milne Dam Conservation Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/milne-dam/): I come out here for the wide water and the meadow grass, thick woods on the far bank and an old dam at the end of the trail.
- [Markham Museum](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/markham-museum/): More than twenty heritage buildings spread over 25 acres, gravel lanes and open fields, and an 1848 church standing at the quiet end.
- [Cathedral of the Transfiguration](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/cathedral-transfiguration/): Three gold onion domes over an open plaza in Markham. I shoot it wide, because the building is the whole point.
- [Mill Pond Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/mill-pond/): A quiet mill pond in old Richmond Hill, ringed by a trail and footbridges, with a boardwalk and a large gazebo on the south shore.
- [Richmond Green Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/richmond-green/): A gazebo on the pond, a rose garden, and a waterfall under an arched bridge, all close enough to shoot in one unhurried loop.
- [Phyllis Rawlinson Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/phyllis-rawlinson/): A farmhouse from about 1830 and its barn, York Region's oldest designated buildings, with moraine woodland behind them. I shoot the last light here.
- [Richmond Hill Heritage Centre](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/rh-heritage-centre/): An 1840 Regency cottage with a white gazebo on landscaped grounds behind it, a small park that can be worked end to end inside one permit block.
- [Gairloch Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/gairloch-gardens/): A Tudor stone house above Lake Ontario, with rose beds and a pond on the slope below it and open water at the foot of the lawn.
- [Erchless Estate](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/erchless-estate/): The founding family's 1858 house above Oakville Harbour, with broad lawns, stone walls, a 1920s rock garden and stairs down to Sixteen Mile Creek.
- [Bronte Heritage Waterfront Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/bronte-harbour/): Masts and fishing boats along the harbour wall, a short pier out to the lighthouse, and the lake wide open behind it.
- [Coronation Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/coronation-park-oakville/): A wide pebble beach open to Lake Ontario, with mature shade trees and long lawns holding soft light just behind it.
- [Graydon Hall Manor](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/graydon-hall/): A 1936 fieldstone manor on the brow of a hill, its 160 foot stone terrace looking down over fountains and formal gardens.
- [Paletta Lakefront Park and Mansion](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/paletta/): An estate house on fourteen acres of Burlington lakefront, a wooded creek folded in behind it and Lake Ontario at the end of the lawn.
- [LaSalle Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/lasalle-park/): A sheltered bay on Burlington's Aldershot side, a 1917 pavilion above the water, and masts clinking at the marina a short walk down the slope.
- [Albion Falls](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/albion-falls/): Red Hill Creek steps down the escarpment in wide shelves, loud in spring and gold in October, and you hear it before you clear the parking lot.
- [Princess Point](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/princess-point/): A low sand point where Cootes Paradise opens up to the west, tall prairie grass at your backs and the whole marsh holding the last of the light.
- [Sam Lawrence Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/sam-lawrence/): A stone lookout on the escarpment brow where the lower city, the harbour and Lake Ontario all open up behind you at golden hour.
- [Parkwood National Historic Site](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/parkwood-estate/): A 1917 auto baron's mansion in Oshawa, eleven acres of heritage gardens around it, fountains and mature evergreens that hold light late in the day.
- [Lakeview Park](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/lakeview-park-oshawa/): A sand beach, a pier running out into Lake Ontario, and three nineteenth century heritage houses a short walk back from the water.
- [Oshawa Valley Botanical Gardens](https://kashklicks.ca/location-guide/oshawa-botanical/): In June this creek valley fills with more than three hundred varieties of peonies, and the Memory Garden walkways lead to a pergola given by the Rotary Clubs.
